solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Withhold advance payment associated with land area

parts.note: a sub is an advance on wages
a tract is a stretch of land

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to hand over a deposit tied up with a plot of land.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away or deduct, so withholding part of a sum is subtracting it.

clue.text: One embroiled in terrible fuss over mass mystic belief

indicators.note: in a down answer, over means the first part sits above the next
embroiled in means caught up inside the jumble
terrible signals the word fuss is mixed up

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone caught up in an awful row over a mass-based mystic faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' turns FUSS into SUFS, and I goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Sufism is the mystical tradition within Islam, a belief system centred on inner union with God.

clue.text: Treasure finally found in half- covered gold chest

indicators.note: found in means the letter is discovered inside the other pieces
half means only the first three letters of the six-letter synonym are used

parts.note: buried means covered over
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word treasure

explanation.surface: Treasure turns up in a chest of gold that was half buried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-' cuts BURIED to BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A bureau is a chest of drawers or writing desk, a piece of furniture for storage.

clue.text: Confluence of three rivers that's astonishing

indicators.note: a confluence is where rivers meet, so the Ouse flows in between the two R's

parts.note: two of the three rivers are R, the abbreviation for river
the third river is the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and in East Anglia

explanation.surface: Where three rivers meet is quite a sight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is an English river, set between two Rs.
explanation.definitionFit: A rouser is something that stirs or startles people, a thing that astonishes.

clue.text: Substitute to stick close, tackling fit winger from Eire

indicators.note: tackling means taking hold of, so the clinging word grips the rest

parts.note: to cling is to stick close
the hang of a garment is how it fits

indicators.note: a winger is at the edge, here the first letter of Eire

explanation.surface: A substitute is told to stay close and tackle a fit Irish winger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit' is a noun, the way clothes hang; 'winger' is the edge letter of Eire, not a footballer.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a changeling is a fairy child secretly left in place of a human baby, a substitute.

clue.text: Oddly themed wrapping around stale sweet

indicators.note: the odd letters are wrapped about the synonym for stale, enclosing it
oddly asks for the first, third and fifth letters of themed

parts.note: food gone off is stale

explanation.surface: A themed wrapper is put round a sweet that has gone stale.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter, a classic sweet.

clue.text: John to be working thus?

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Is John meant to be busy like this?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: anyone working on John's rearranged letters would be at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at work, busy doing their job, is said to be working in this way.

clue.text: Against one's will, fob Cyril off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone fobs Cyril off against his will.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something forcibly means doing it by force, overriding a person's wishes.

clue.text: All that stored in a big mountain? No way

indicators.note: stored in means placed inside
no means without, so the road abbreviation is removed

parts.note: Everest is the biggest mountain of all
ST is short for street, a way
yon is an old word for that

explanation.surface: Everything is stored inside a huge mountain? No way!
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' looks like an exclamation of disbelief, but it tells you to drop the abbreviation for street.
explanation.definitionFit: Everyone means all the people, the whole lot.

clue.text: Recipes showing full fat evenly filling moulds

indicators.note: the even letters go inside the synonym for moulds, filling it

parts.note: forms are moulds that shape things

indicators.note: evenly asks for the second, fourth and sixth letters of the words full fat

explanation.surface: Recipes call for full-fat ingredients spread evenly into moulds.
explanation.definitionFit: A formula is a set method or prescription, so recipes are formulae for dishes.

clue.text: Bow before English writer

parts.note: read as 'what the bow comes before': on a ship the bow is at the front and the rear end follows it

explanation.surface: Someone bows before an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow before' is a riddle: the part of a boat that has the bow in front of it is its rear. Several blog commenters thought it a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne, the eighteenth-century novelist who wrote Tristram Shandy, was a writer.

clue.text: Doctor Solomon perhaps mentioned these days?

indicators.note: mentioned means the words are spoken, so the spoken form counts

parts.note: to doctor an animal is to spay it, and Solomon is the model of a sage

explanation.surface: Is there a Doctor Solomon being talked about nowadays?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, to neuter an animal; Solomon is an example of a wise man.
explanation.definitionFit: The space age is the modern era of rockets and satellites, the present times.

clue.text: Mysteriously, Turkish change about the old revolutionary guards

indicators.note: the reversed old word stands either side of the other piece, guarding it
revolutionary means turned over, so the old word is written backwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the coins are read backwards

parts.note: lire, plural of lira, are Turkish coins, loose change

explanation.surface: A shifting Turkish coin is guarded by an old revolutionary, which is strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns LIRE into ERIL; 'revolutionary' turns YE into EY, which then 'guards' ERIL. Chambers allows lire as a plural of lira.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerily means in a strange, uncanny way, the same as mysteriously.

clue.text: Decode a single foreign dash

parts.note: un is French for a, one
to dash is to scramble, rush

explanation.surface: Decipher one foreign dash in a coded message.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a coded message is to unscramble it, putting its parts back into readable order.

clue.text: Galleon rebuilt in outskirts of local northern British town

indicators.note: the outskirts of a word are its first and last letters
rebuilt means the ship's letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: A galleon is reconstructed on the edge of a local northern town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuilt' shuffles the ship together with the two edge letters of local; they cannot simply surround it.
explanation.definitionFit: Llangollen is a town in north Wales, famous for its international music eisteddfod.

clue.text: Mike is lazy, disheartened about software being put to bad use?

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet
an app is a piece of software

indicators.note: disheartened means the heart is taken out, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: Mike is idle and downhearted about software misused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' only joins: the software comes before the shortened lazy in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To misapply something is to use it wrongly, for an improper purpose.

clue.text: Extremely unnerving school punishment imposed on son, nasty character

indicators.note: in a down answer, imposed on means placed above the next piece
extremely asks for the outermost letters of the word unnerving

parts.note: lines are a punishment, sentences written out over and over

explanation.surface: A cruel school punishment inflicted on a son shows a nasty streak.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugliness is unpleasantness or offensiveness of nature, a nasty character.

clue.text: Ordered ruddy fish to be served up for tea

indicators.note: an order is spoken, so the word is taken as it sounds

parts.note: rosy means ruddy, pink-cheeked

indicators.note: in a down answer, served up means written upwards, backwards

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A rosy fish is ordered to be served at teatime.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog takes ROSIE as a sound-alike of rosy; 'Ordered' is the only word left to signal it. Rosie Lee is Cockney rhyming slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang, a Rosie Lee rhymes with and so stands for a cup of tea.

clue.text: Pleasing to sport trendy snip and trim

indicators.note: to sport is to wear, so the word for pleasing wears the word for trendy in front of it

parts.note: in means fashionable
good means pleasing
a nick is a small cut, a snip

explanation.surface: It's nice to wear a fashionable cut and a neat trim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trim' is an adjective here, meaning in fine condition, not the hairdresser's noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in good nick is in good condition, fit and shipshape, which is what trim means.

clue.text: Frank, dry, on alcohol following vacation

indicators.note: in a down answer, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne

indicators.note: vacation means emptying, so the word alcohol is emptied, keeping only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Frank on the drink after a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation' looks like a holiday but means emptying out.
explanation.definitionFit: Brutal honesty is blunt and harsh, so frank in the sense of unsparing.

clue.text: Most of solvers are tense about good food

indicators.note: about means around, so the other letters go round the G
most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: you're, from you are, addresses the solvers
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Solvers tend to be tense about good food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' cuts YOURE to YOUR; adding T gives YOURT, wrapped about G.
explanation.definitionFit: Yogurt, fermented milk, is a food.

clue.text: Eats out, vomits, runs off

indicators.note: off means the runs abbreviation is removed

parts.note: retches means tries to vomit
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone dines out, throws up and races off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eats out' is the verb for acid corroding a surface, not a restaurant meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid etches metal by eating away its surface.

clue.text: Detectives barricading main road caught tart

indicators.note: barricading means the detectives block the road, standing in the middle of it

parts.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI in crosswords
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK police detectives
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Police barricade a main road and catch a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; the digit 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tart is sour, with the sharp taste of acid.

clue.text: Cycling your vehicle, going outside for effect

indicators.note: the vehicle goes round the outside of the cycled letters

parts.note: a cart is a simple vehicle

indicators.note: cycling moves the first letter of the word your round to the end

explanation.surface: Rotating your vehicle as it heads outside for effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'effect' is the verb, to bring about, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To effect something, as a verb, is to accomplish or execute it.

clue.text: Losing temperature, spread everything around dish

indicators.note: losing means a letter is dropped from the spread

parts.note: pâté is a spread for toast

indicators.note: around means turned about, so the word for everything is read backwards

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: Going cold, spread everything around the dish.
explanation.walkthrough: The spread is pâté, written without its accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish with seafood or chicken, cooked in a wide pan.

clue.text: OTT addiction not initially associated with rejected heroin

indicators.note: not initially means the letter that opens the word for addiction is not left at the start but shifted along

parts.note: a habit is an addiction

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: cum, Latin for with, links two things combined, as in bed-cum-sitting-room
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A wildly excessive addiction that has nothing to do with heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: Read plainly: HABIT loses its first letter, 'rejected' turns CUM into MUC, and H for heroin ends it; the H that leaves the front is the one that returns at the end. OTT stands for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Something over the top is excessive, rather too much, the idiom for overdoing it.

clue.text: Who'd agree no women should be in opposition?

definitions.text: Who'd agree no women should be in opposition?

parts.words: Who'd agree no women should be in opposition?
parts.note: people who always agree say yes; and the phrase is the exact opposite of no women, yes against no and men against women

explanation.surface: Who would back a ban on women in the opposition party?
explanation.walkthrough: Swap each word of 'no women' for its opposite and you get the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sycophants who always agree with their boss are known by this phrase.

clue.text: Old tools fixed holes in bottom of boat

indicators.note: fixed means put right, so the letters are reworked
the bottom of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: The holes in the bottom of the boat have been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' shuffles HOLES, IN and T, the last letter of boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoliths are Stone Age implements from the New Stone Age, so ancient tools.
